extracted.intended_audience: State Exchanges, HHS/CMS contractors, QHP issuers, web-brokers, agents/brokers, State Medicaid agencies, health policy stakeholders and commenters on the proposed rule
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory changes and standards governing Exchanges, QHP certification, eligibility/verification, payment programs (risk adjustment, user fees, APTC/CSR), network adequacy, EHB, quality improvement strategy, and enforcement; intended to solicit public comment under the notice-and-comment process.

rubrics_metrics.name: User fee rates for FFEs and SBE-FPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose the 2027 benefit year FFE and SBE-FP user fee rates of 2.5 percent and 2.0 percent of total monthly premiums, respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets the percent-of-premium user fee rates to be applied for the 2027 benefit year on the Federal platform and State-based exchanges on the Federal platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'eligible noncitizen' for BHP
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to add a new definition of 'eligible noncitizen' at 42 CFR 600.5, cross-referencing 45 CFR 155.20, to align Basic Health Program (BHP) regulations with section 71301 of the WFTC legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Federal BHP payments are based in part on PTC eligibility, only lawfully present noncitizens considered 'eligible aliens' will generate Federal BHP payments to the State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequestration of HHS-operated risk adjustment payments
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS-operated risk adjustment program will sequester payments made from fiscal year 2026 resources at a rate of 5.7 percent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies sequestration consistent with OMB Report to Congress and BBEDCA; sequestered funds may become available for payment in the following fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalibration of 2027 risk adjustment models
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to recalibrate the 2027 benefit year HHS risk adjustment models using the 2021, 2022, and 2023 benefit year enrollee-level EDGE data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicits comment on whether to retain separate risk adjustment transfer calculations for individual catastrophic and non-catastrophic plans under the State payment transfer formula.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment user fee rate
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose a risk adjustment user fee rate for the 2027 benefit year of $0.20 per member per month (PMPM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the per-member-per-month fee to support HHS-operated risk adjustment administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS-RADV error estimation modification
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to modify one intermediate step of the HHS-RADV error estimation methodology starting with 2025 benefit year HHS-RADV to add an additional scaling factor to appropriately estimate the proportion of the issuer's total plan liability risk score (PLRS) that is HCC-related after removal of no HCC enrollees from the IVA sample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodological change follows prior finalization in the 2026 Payment Notice and addresses IVA sample composition changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: CSR loading disclosure in URRTs and Actuarial Memoranda
rubrics_metrics.description: Require issuers that intend to load rates to account for unpaid CSRs for the applicable rating year to submit certain information related to CSR loading in their Unified Rate Review Templates (URRTs) and the Actuarial Memoranda for each filing year beginning with PY 2027 rate filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adds reporting/transparency obligations for insurers when CSRs are not funded and they 'load' rates to account for unpaid CSRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove one-plan-year SBE-FP prerequisite for State Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove the requirement at §155.105(b)(4) that a State seeking to operate a State Exchange must first operate an SBE-FP for at least one plan year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates the prior step intended to demonstrate State operational experience before full State Exchange operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind State Exchange Blueprint progress documentation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.106(a)(2) to rescind the requirement that a State must provide supporting documentation demonstrating progress toward meeting State Exchange Blueprint requirements as part of establishment activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: CMS already collects supporting documentation through preexisting Blueprint Application processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: State-required benefits considered 'in addition to EHB' criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §155.170(a) to provide that beginning with PY 2027, a State-required benefit would be considered 'in addition to EHB' if it: (1) is required by a State action taking place after December 31, 2011; (2) is applicable to the small group and/or individual markets; (3) is specific to required care, treatment, or services; and (4) is not required by State action for purposes of compliance with Federal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under this proposal, such State-required benefits would be considered in addition to EHB regardless of whether embedded in the State's EHB-benchmark plan; conforming revisions to §§155.170(a)(2) and 156.115(a) proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange centralized eligibility/enrollment interface options
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose amendments to §155.205(b) to allow a State Exchange to either operate a centralized eligibility and enrollment consumer interface on its website or provide that functionality exclusively through one or more State Exchange-approved consumer websites operated by a web-broker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits flexibility for how consumers may submit a single streamlined eligibility application and subsequently select a QHP following determination of eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: New SBE-EDE option (exclusive web-broker pathway)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose at §155.221(k) that State Exchanges may elect a new EDE option (SBE-EDE) to allow web-brokers to operate enrollment websites as the exclusive pathway for application, eligibility determination, and purchase of an individual market QHP offered through the Exchange with APTC and CSRs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires HHS approval and that consumers be otherwise eligible; creates an option where web-brokers are the exclusive consumer-facing enrollment pathway.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory HHS-approved consumer consent form for agents/brokers/web-brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose changes requiring agents, brokers, and web-brokers to use an HHS-approved and created consumer consent form to meet eligibility application review and consumer consent documentation requirements, eliminating flexibility to use their own templates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also propose clarifying what constitutes a consumer 'taking an action' for eligibility review/confirmation and consumer consent; require these entities to provide HHS marketing documentation during monitoring, audit, and enforcement; hold them responsible for marketing content produced on their behalf; and add prohibited marketing practice examples at §155.220(j)(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discontinue vendor program for certain training/verification functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose removing §155.222 to discontinue the vendor program that allowed certain training and information verification functions to be provided by HHS-approved vendors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates the ability to outsource these functions to approved vendors under current regulatory framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align Exchange eligibility/verification with WFTC 'eligible alien' rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose updates to §§155.20, 155.305(f)(1), and 155.320 to align Exchange regulations with section 71301 of the WFTC legislation, adding a new definition and updating APTC eligibility and verification rules so that PTC is allowed for lawfully present noncitizens only if such noncitizen is an 'eligible alien.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also impacts Federal payments to States for BHP enrollments of lawfully present noncitizens who are not 'eligible aliens,' effective January 1, 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Align APTC eligibility with WFTC §71302 (remove §155.305(f)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: To align with section 71302 of the WFTC legislation, propose removing §155.305(f)(2) and making conforming updates to §§155.320(c)(3)(iii)(A) and 155.420(d)(13), reflecting that PTC is no longer allowed for certain lawfully present noncitizens with household income below 100% FPL who were ineligible for Medicaid due to immigration status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change also affects Federal payments to States for applicable BHP individuals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Failure-to-file-and-reconcile policy (1-year vs 2-year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose revising §155.305(f)(4) such that Exchanges on the Federal platform would conduct the 1-year policy beginning in PY 2027; State Exchanges could choose 1- or 2-year in PY 2027 but must conduct 1-year beginning PY 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the 1-year policy an Exchange must determine a tax filer ineligible for APTC if HHS notifies that the filer received APTC for a prior year used for verification and the filer did not file a Federal tax return and reconcile APTC for that year; proposing to remove a notice requirement for PY 2027 to conform with PY 2026 policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek comment on implementation considerations for WFTC verification requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comment on operational considerations, rollout and communications, timelines, complexity, costs, burden, enrollment impacts, and State-specific considerations for future policy development and implementation under section 71303 of the WFTC legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for input to inform implementation of new Exchange eligibility verification requirements imposed by WFTC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continue income verification changes and create DMIs when trusted data indicates income <100% FPL
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise §155.320(c) so all Exchanges must continue income verification changes introduced in the 2025 Marketplace Integrity and Affordability final rule in PY 2027 and beyond; specifically update §155.320(c)(3)(iii) and (c)(3)(vi)(C)(2) to extend requirement to create income data matching issues (DMIs) when trusted data sources indicate projected household income under 100% FPL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also propose removing §155.320(c)(5), which previously required accepting annual household income attestation when no tax data is returned for a household.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit comment on issuer premium-payment threshold options
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek comment on whether HHS should regulate the option for issuers to implement fixed-dollar and/or gross percentage-based premium payment thresholds in §155.400(g) for PY 2027 and beyond (issuers currently may only implement a net premium percentage-based threshold for PY 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Asks for feedback on whether to authorize additional threshold options effective January 1, 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit 150 percent FPL SEP
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove §155.420(d)(16) such that Exchanges would continue to be prohibited from offering the 150 percent FPL Special Enrollment Period (SEP) in PY 2027 and beyond, aligning with section 71304 of the WFTC legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes conforming amendments to related paragraphs in §155.420.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Enrollment Period Verification (SEPV) scope and minimum coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise §155.420(g) to remove the restriction limiting Exchanges on the Federal platform to only conduct SEPV for Loss of Minimum Essential Coverage (MEC), and to require Exchanges on the Federal platform to conduct SEPV for at least 75 percent of new enrollments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions were finalized previously but stayed in litigation (City of Columbus v. Kennedy); HHS is reproposing them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand hardship exemption eligibility for catastrophic coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.605 to allow individuals who are ineligible for APTC or CSRs due to projected household income below 100% or above 250% of the FPL to qualify for a hardship exemption under §155.605(d)(1)(iii); individuals aged 30+ receiving this exemption may enroll in catastrophic coverage if otherwise eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broadens the circumstances under which a hardship exemption is available to permit catastrophic plan enrollment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modify network adequacy standards and reviews for State Exchanges
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.1050(a)(2) to remove requirements that State Exchanges and SBE-FPs establish and impose quantitative time and distance network adequacy standards at least as stringent as those for QHPs on FFEs and to no longer require quantitative network adequacy reviews prior to certifying a plan; instead require State Exchanges to ensure QHPs provide sufficient access consistent with §156.230 (or proposed §156.236 for non-network plans).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also propose deferring provider access reviews of QHP issuers applying for FFE certification to FFE States that elect to conduct such reviews and can demonstrate 'Effective Provider Access Review Program' criteria under proposed §155.1050(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Essential Community Provider (ECP) Review Program requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose adding §155.1051 to allow FFE States to elect to conduct their own ECP certification reviews of issuers (with or without a provider network) applying for certification to be offered as QHPs through an FFE; FFE States would need to demonstrate sufficient authority and technical capacity to conduct reviews per applicable criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets standards and expectations for State capacity and authority before delegating ECP certification review responsibilities to States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allow SEIPM to satisfy independent external programmatic audit requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §155.1200(d) and add paragraph (e) to permit State Exchanges to satisfy certain independent external programmatic audit requirements by completing the SEIPM process established at 45 CFR 155, subpart Q.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SEIPM relates to measuring improper payments of APTC administered by State Exchanges to satisfy PIIA requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establish SEIPM program to measure improper APTC payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose adding new subpart Q (§§155.1600 through 1650) to establish the SEIPM program to measure improper payments of APTC administered by State Exchanges and to annually report statistically valid improper payment estimates in the HHS Agency Financial Report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implements Payment Integrity Information Act (PIIA) requirements for programs susceptible to improper payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pause review of State EHB-benchmark plan selection applications
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS is pausing review of State applications to select EHB-benchmark plans in accordance with §156.111 while reviewing section 1302 of the ACA and considering future rulemaking to revise §156.111 and EHB standards more broadly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals potential future substantive changes to EHB selection rules and pause on application processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibit routine non-pediatric dental as EHB
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise §156.115(d) to prohibit issuers from including routine non-pediatric dental services as an Essential Health Benefit (EHB).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes what services may be counted as part of EHB beginning in the applicable plan year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catastrophic plan multi-year terms and V-BID for preventive services
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to modify §156.155 to specify a catastrophic plan may have a plan term of 1 year, or multiple consecutive years not to exceed 10 years; catastrophic plans with terms of at least 2 years may utilize value-based insurance designs (V-BID) to offer benefits for preventive services without requiring beneficiaries to first satisfy their deductible or annual cost-sharing limitation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also propose changes to §156.130 for how annual limitation on cost sharing applies over the life of a multi-year contract (monthly division), and to §156.80 to permit plan-level adjustment to the index rate reflecting term length.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise permissible cost-sharing parameters for bronze and catastrophic plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose new §156.136 for permissible cost-sharing parameters for individual market bronze plans and revise §156.155(a)(3) for required cost-sharing parameters for catastrophic plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses implementation issues related to cost-sharing parameter provisions in section 1302(c)-(e) of the ACA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remove standardized plan options and related requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to remove definition of 'standardized options' at §155.20; remove requirements pertaining to standardized plan options at §156.201; remove differential display and related requirements at §§155.205(b)(1), 155.220(c)(3)(i)(H), and 156.265(b)(3)(iv); discontinue annual design/publication of standardized plan options and non-standardized plan option limits/exceptions at §156.202 effective PY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminates the standardized plan option program and associated display and limit mechanisms on the Federal platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provider network requirement for QHPs and new non-network plan pathway
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to revise §156.230 and §156.235 to clarify these sections contain provider access standards for QHPs and SADPs that use a network and to remove the requirement that all QHPs must use a network of providers. Add new §156.236 to allow non-network plans to receive QHP certification by demonstrating sufficient choice of providers that accept the plan's benefit amount as payment in full and reasonable/timely access to ECPs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes standards and a certification pathway for non-network plans and clarifies applicability of access standards across plan types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lower ECP contracting minimums (35% to 20%)
rubrics_metrics.description: For PY 2027 and subsequent plan years, propose reducing the minimum percentage requirement from 35 to 20 percent for both medical QHP and SADP issuers, and separately at least 20 percent of available FQHCs and 20 percent of available family planning providers that qualify as ECPs in each plan's service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also propose modifying narrative justification requirements at §§156.235(a)(3) and (b)(3) to align with systems and submission processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS authority for issuer audits and compliance reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to modify §156.480(c) to clarify HHS' authority to audit or conduct compliance reviews of issuers offering QHPs through an Exchange for purposes of administering and providing oversight of the APTC, CSR, and user fee programs, and to permit such reviews to be conducted as needed or on an annual basis rather than only ad hoc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands clarity on auditing authority and potential frequency of reviews tied to these programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors and lawful purposes considered in CMP amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose amending §156.805(b) to reiterate that HHS, in determining CMP amounts, will identify the lawful purpose(s) of the CMP and take into account enumerated factors listed in §156.805(b)(1)-(3); propose conforming edits to §150.317 to reflect this approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies that lawful purposes are to be identified and listed factors applied as appropriate when assessing CMPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative law judge subpoena authority and procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §156.903 to provide the option for an administrative law judge (ALJ) to issue subpoenas, on the ALJ's own motion or at request of a party, if reasonably necessary for full presentation of a case, and to add procedures governing issuing subpoenas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expands procedural tools available in administrative hearings concerning QHP/CMP matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery limitations for administrative appeals of CMPs identified via audits
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to amend §156.935 to ensure that the discovery provisions set forth do not apply to administrative appeals of proposed CMPs for violations identified through audits of the APTC, CSR, or user fee programs under §156.480(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limits discovery in specific CMP administrative appeals arising from program audits.

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP Quality Improvement Strategy (QIS) submission requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to require QHP issuers to submit Quality Improvement Strategies (QISs) addressing any two of the five topic areas listed in section 1311(g)(1) of the ACA, without mandating which specific topic areas an issuer must address, beginning with PY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Makes QIS statutory certification requirement more flexible by allowing issuers to choose two of five topic areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Netting CMPs across affiliates and basis for calculating debt
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose amending §156.1215(b) so CMPs assessed against health coverage issuers and their affiliates under the same TIN would be subject to netting as part of HHS' integrated monthly payment and collection cycle; propose amending §156.1215(c) so amounts owed by an issuer and affiliates after netting would be the basis for calculating debt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes how CMPs are aggregated/netted across related entities and affects debt calculation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solicit comment on adjusting Federal MLR standard in States
rubrics_metrics.description: Solicit comment on the impact of the Federal Medical Loss Ratio (MLR) standard on individual market stability and whether HHS should use its authority under section 2718(b)(1)(A)(ii) of the PHS Act and §158.301 to adjust the MLR standard in a State to promote individual market stability; also solicit comment on how to amend regulations to allow States to request MLR adjustments more easily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for stakeholder input on whether and how to adjust MLR standards to address State-level market stability concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS risk adjustment model inputs and PLRS use
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS risk adjustment models predict plan liability for an average enrollee based on age, sex, and diagnoses (HCCs), producing a risk score; enrollment-weighted average risk score (PLRS) within a geographic rating area is an input into the State payment transfer formula determining State transfer payments or charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains model structure (adult/child/infant models, RXCs, ACFs, enrollment duration factors) and how PLRS is used in State transfer calculations.
